subject: Physics
standard_explanation: A magnet produces a magnetic field that exerts force on ferromagnetic materials such as iron, cobalt, and nickel. Every magnet has two distinct poles: a North-seeking pole (N) and a South-seeking pole (S). The fundamental law of magnetic poles states that unlike (opposite) poles attract each other, whereas like (similar) poles repel each other.
simplified_explanation: Magnets are like magical friends with special hugs! Every magnet has two sides: a North pole (Red) and a South pole (Blue). When a Red pole meets a Blue pole, snap! They hug together (Attract). But when two Red poles face each other, whoosh! They push each other away (Repel)!
key_points: Every magnet has two poles: North (N) and South (S).
Opposite poles attract: North and South pull together.
Similar poles repel: North pushes North away; South pushes South away.
Magnets attract metals like iron, steel, and nickel, but not wood or plastic.
examples: Refrigerator magnets sticking firmly to the metal fridge door.
A magnetic compass needle pointing toward Earth's magnetic north pole.
misconceptions: Misconception: If you cut a magnet in half, you get a separate North pole and South pole. Fact: Cutting a magnet creates two smaller complete magnets, each with its own North and South poles.
Misconception: Magnets stick to all metals like aluminum or gold. Fact: Magnets only attract ferromagnetic metals like iron and steel.

visual_scenes.title: Bar Magnet Poles
visual_scenes.description: A classic red (North) and blue (South) bar magnet rests on a table with clear pole labels.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 1: Every magnet has two ends: a North pole (N) and a South pole (S).

visual_scenes.title: Opposite Poles Attract!
visual_scenes.description: North (Red) faces South (Blue). Magnetic flux lines snap them together with spark stars.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Opposite poles love each other! North and South pull together (Attract)!

visual_scenes.title: Like Poles Repel!
visual_scenes.description: North (Red) faces North (Red). An invisible magnetic force pushes them apart.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Same poles push away! North pushes North away (Repel)!

sign_glossary.description: Bent C-handshapes pull together sharply, miming magnetic stickiness.
sign_glossary.movement: Hands snap together with a firm clasp

sign_glossary.description: Both open hands facing inward pull towards each other rapidly.
Palms facing each other push forcefully apart in opposite directions.
